svg.text: From "my game is broken" to "the fix is in the repository"
The assistant never changes anything on its own: it writes the plan, the player says yes, the fix is verified on the device.
the game breaks
"RDR is black after the intro"
the player says what they see;
the assistant goes and looks
the case opens
one file per game, on the phone:
symptom, cause, plan, evidence,
and a timeline the player can read
the diagnosis
the game's own logs, the knowledge
base (offline), then the upstream's
pull requests if the network allows
the plan
symptom → cause → proposed fix,
with the evidence that named it, in
the player's own language
the player says yes
only now does the assistant touch
code — the originals are kept, the
diff is computed from them
verified on the device
the runtime is rebuilt, the game runs again,
and the numbers are written down: shaders found,
draws per frame, frames per second, the log lines
"the second renderer driven by a host thread"
contribute upstream
one button packs the case into a zip:
the case document, the files that changed,
the manifest and the diff — no game files,
no keys; the packer refuses them
the game graduates
the case lands as a pull request, the maintainer reads
the diff, the profile and the android.tsv follow, and the
game is counted in the list of the games that run.
the credit goes to whoever opened the case
seven games came out of this pipe
Every row is a real case file on a player's phone, with the fix on a branch in the repository and the numbers in the commit message.
Red Dead Redemption
the shader split found 0 shaders (Rockstar's encrypted RPF6 archives) → 3,628;
the screen stayed black after the intro (a second audio renderer) → the title screen
Fire Emblem: Three Houses
the game died silently 1.8 s after launch → it renders the class demo
STAR OCEAN THE SECOND STORY R
the GPU was lost 4 minutes into the menu (one huge submission) → the fix is in;
the player's own ten-minute run decides
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter
the whole scene was black (a texture builder that answered nothing) → the world draws
TMNT: Shredder's Revenge
it died at start-up (the online SDK was refused) → it boots to the menu
Octopath Traveler II
the Unreal allocator asked for blocks the host could not give → the fix is in;
the device run is the player's next step
Bayonetta 3
the shaders live in PKZ archives (Oodle, one entry at a time) → it runs on the phone
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
the DLC and the shared CJK font were missing from the pack → a case is open
The player's part is small: press yes, or say no.
The assistant's part is the diagnosis, the patch and the verification.
Neither of them needed to know how a shader is built —
the knowledge was already written down, and it ships
with the app.
